## 9cd1c439ddccc3ea · other · high · open

**Fact:** A ship that never received a verdict AT ALL can never be re-graded, because regradable_ships() selects on an EXISTING verdict's red gates - 'A ship is re-gradable only when every CI job its verdict's RED gates map to is success' - so a ticket with zero runner_verdicts rows is invisible to it permanently. AGT-609 (delivered) fixed the adjacent case, a ship blocked under grading rules that later changed; it does not reach the zero-verdict case. Measured live 2026-11-09: AGT-552 has zero verdicts, regradable_ships() returned 87 other refs and not AGT-552, and the settle therefore refuses delivered for want of a verdict and falls to partial + a gated card. The cause of the missing verdict is named in decision f348e89b: each of these builds adds its OWN regression test, which is absent from the pre-build baseline the verdict grades against, so 7a could record nothing. At least three tickets sit in this state (AGT-552, AGT-519, AGT-547), each with its fix verified on dev and its own test passing, and each reaching John as a gated card asking for a verdict no automatic path can supply.

**Locations:**
- `scripts/verifier.js --regrade (refusal text)` — "public.regradable_ships()"
- `runner_cycles:d006ab42-ae60-4bcf-ab30-e951ab4cea99 (measured 2026-11-09)` — "verifier --regrade: public.regradable_ships() did not return AGT-552"
- `runner_decisions:f348e89b-03c3-41a4-8a70-899b2f24a075 (reasoning)` — "step 7a could record no verdict (every one of those builds adds its own regression test, which is absent from the pre-build baseline the verdict grades against), so settle-ship refuses the delivered status"
- `backlog_items:AGT-609 (delivered)` — "A ship blocked under grading rules that later change is never graded again, so delivered work piles up behind verdicts nobody can regrade"

**Proposed resolution:** Give the zero-verdict case a grading path that does not require re-measuring a baseline on an already-built tree: either let regradable_ships() admit a ship with NO verdict whose commit is an ancestor of dev and whose related tests pass in the newest ref='dev' CI conclusion, or make the pre-build baseline record the test files the kickoff declares it will ADD so 7a can grade a build that brings its own test. Assert both directions: a zero-verdict delivered ship becomes gradable and settles delivered with a ship decision, and a genuinely red ship is still refused.

**Ruling:** stopLineClosesPartial()'s step 3 returns true for any STOP LINE sentence carrying the word 'partial' and no ticket id -- 'the ship speaking about itself'. A kickoff whose subject IS partial-settling describes the behaviour in exactly that shape, so AGT-595's own v7.0.980 STOP LINE ('a refused `delivered` settles `partial` and files a `gated_before_build` card') settled its own finished ship partial: planShip() was skipped, the shipped change carries zero kind='ship' decisions and therefore no Reverse handle, and the row stayed re-pickable until a later cycle spent a Designer pass rediscovering the work was done. ## 22d85ed47e15371c · other · high · ticketed

**Fact:** A check every browser reader calls over /rest/v1/rpc must answer inside the statement timeout; audit_flow_checks() spends 6.7 of its 7.6 seconds inside runner_should_boot(), so any growth in the boot gate silently takes the whole audit rpc offline with a transport error rather than a finding.

**Locations:**
- `public.audit_flow_checks()` — "EXPLAIN ANALYZE 2026-11-09: Execution Time 7560 ms, shared hit 6,445,878 -- PostgREST cancelled the rpc at its statement timeout (HTTP 500, SQLSTATE 57014) before AGT-463's index remediation and sits just under it after"
- `public.runner_should_boot()` — "EXPLAIN ANALYZE 2026-11-09: Execution Time 6733 ms, shared hit 6,441,054 -- 89% of audit_flow_checks()'s whole cost is this one call, made from block (e)"
- `docs/design/agt-496-outcome-check.sql` — "block (e) flow-nothing-produced reads ((SELECT detail FROM public.runner_should_boot())->>'pickable_count')"

**Proposed resolution:** Stop block (e) calling runner_should_boot() for one scalar: either read pickable_count from a cheaper source, or make runner_should_boot() cheap (6.4M buffer hits for one jsonb says an unindexed scan dominates it too). Measured by AGT-463's guard, which reported a transport incident instead of a verdict until an index brought the total back under the timeout.

**Ruling:** Block (e) of public.audit_flow_checks() reads a single scalar -- ((SELECT detail FROM public.runner_should_boot())->>'pickable_count') -- and runner_should_boot() re-evaluates the whole prime_directive_queue CTE to produce it. Measured again this turn: the rpc costs 6,786.9 ms and 6,475,897 shared buffer hits, of which runner_should_boot() alone is 6,576.9 ms and 6,437,759 -- 97%, not the 89% the finding estimated. The gate the browser hits is tighter than the finding assumes: pg_roles shows anon with statement_timeout 3s and authenticated with 8s, so for every reader holding the anon key that ships in the bundle this rpc is already 2.3x over its limit and returns HTTP 500 / SQLSTATE 57014 instead of a verdict. Any further growth in the boot gate takes the audit offline with a transport error rather than a finding, which is the one failure mode a check must not have. / Two steps, narrowest first (pattern:65). (1) Stop block (e) calling runner_should_boot() for one number: read it as `select count(*) from public.prime_directive_queue() q where q.lane in ('drain','selfbuild')`. The lane filter is load-bearing and is the one correction to make to the obvious form: runner_should_boot()'s own `pickable` CTE filters those two lanes, so a bare count(*) over the queue returns 25 where the gate's pickable_count is 24 -- a cheaper source that quietly disagrees is worse than the slow one. (2) Then make the queue itself cheap, because step 1 alone leaves only ~0.8 s of margin under anon's 3 s: its 2.04M buffer hits are per-row function calls over all 1,475 backlog rows -- effective_need_score(), ticket_noship_cycles(), claim_exclusion_reason(), epic_project_executing() -- plus SubPlan 7, which scans backlog_items_epic_id_idx 1,475 times for a `M_ design gate%` title and spends 92,690 buffers doing it. Index or prefilter that, and assert the rpc's total under 3 s as the anon role, not as service_role. (architect, 2026-11-09)

**Locations:**
- `public.sweep_decision_windows(uuid,text)` — "line 85 raises through backlog_done_requires_verdict(): AGT-166: AGT-281 cannot be written done over its latest verdict block (38959e02-fdd5-4858-bf19-11fc48fdc5d2) -- so the call finalises NOTHING, for every caller, not just the ticket it stumbles on"
- `backlog_items:AGT-281` — "status delivered; latest verdict block at 2026-10-02 21:03:00Z; latest ship decision at 2026-10-02 09:25:04Z -- the decision PREDATES the block, which is exactly what the AGT-166 guard refuses, and nothing has re-graded it since"
- `cron.job/runner-window-finaliser` — "SES-320's second caller of the same function, so the failure is not confined to a cycle tail: no decision window anywhere finalises while this stands"
- `scripts/regrade-current.js` — "AGT-609 lane ran this cycle and declared AGT-281 UNGRADABLE, never a block: graded at dev HEAD with no unchanged tree to compare against and regression red, so a red cannot be attributed to that delivery -- the one lane that could clear the block correctly declines to"

**Proposed resolution:** Make the sweep skip-and-report a ticket the AGT-166 guard refuses instead of raising through it -- one row per refusal in its return, the record_skip() precedent -- so one stuck ticket costs its own finalisation and not the sweep's. Separately AGT-281 needs a verdict dated at or after its block, which is the regrade lane's or an attended session's call, never an unattended status write.

**Ruling:** public.sweep_decision_windows(uuid,text) loops over every due decision in ONE transaction with no savepoint and no per-row EXCEPTION block (read its pg_get_functiondef this turn: the only `raise exception` is the argument check, and the loop body's `update public.backlog_items set status='done'` fires backlog_done_requires_verdict()). That trigger refuses AGT-281 under its AGT-166 clause -- latest verdict is a block of 2026-10-02 21:03Z with no ship or ticket-status decision dated at or after it -- so the one refusal rolls back every other finalisation for every caller, the cycle tail and cron.job/runner-window-finaliser alike. flow-nothing-produced is the same cause seen from the other end: a drain's only exit is every member written done (AGT-495), so the three fully-settled drain-epic directives cannot retire and no ticket settles done. / Fault-isolate the sweep per decision -- a BEGIN/EXCEPTION block or savepoint around each row, counting and naming the refused ones in the return the way record_skip() already reports a skip -- and leave backlog_done_requires_verdict() exactly as it is: the guard is right, the all-or-nothing statement is the defect. Then run one catch-up sweep and assert both directions. AGT-281 itself needs a verdict dated at or after its block, which is the regrade lane's or an attended session's call and never an unattended status write. (architect, 2026-11-09)

**Fact:** Whether an AGT-609 re-grade moves the trust ladder: the three re-grade verdicts this cycle wrote say 'the ladder not asked', yet the ship decisions they spawned carry ladder_work_class bug_fix unstamped, so 7b will promote bug_fix three times for deliveries whose prior ladder effect was a reset.

- `runner_verdicts:2408c2b7-b598-442a-a9d1-954dba2d1646` — "backlog_id AGT-172, verdict approve, auto_done_eligible false, auto_done_reason: auto-done does not apply to a re-grade (AGT-609): a second look at an existing delivery, the ladder not asked. ladder_applied_at null"
- `public.record_ship_decision(uuid,text,text,text,uuid)` — "v_wc := public.ladder_work_class(v_class); v_dec := public.record_decision( p_cycle_id, NULL, 'ship', p_backlog_id, format('%s shipped at %s (%s) on verdict %s', [...]), v_verdict.reasoning, v_wc );"
- `runner_decisions:6d45a8ba-9fe4-4aa6-a913-b7d92b6a20a0` — "kind ship, backlog_id AGT-172, ladder_work_class bug_fix, ladder_applied_at null, status open (likewise 2c971f59-fcc6-4147-b141-03eb94bc9b8c AGT-176 and 7ece3392-6d1a-4f2d-9830-7f06c078b03a AGT-187)"
- `public.sweep_decision_windows(uuid,text)` — "if r.ladder_work_class is not null and r.ladder_applied_at is null then [...] from public.ladder_apply_signal(r.ladder_work_class, 'promote', p_actor_cycle, p_actor_session);"

**Proposed resolution:** The verdict's rule (regrade-current.js, AGT-609: the ladder not asked) should win: a re-grade's decision is recorded with ladder_work_class NULL, via a flag on record_ship_decision() or a direct record_decision() call, so finalisation moves no rung; SES-315(b)'s reason applies, a second count 'manufactures a rung'.

**Ruling:** public.record_ship_decision() reads the ticket's priority_class off the board and sets v_wc := ladder_work_class(v_class) UNCONDITIONALLY -- its source never reads the verdict's ladder_applied_at or auto_done_eligible, although it already holds the whole verdict row. sweep_decision_windows() then promotes any unstamped ladder_work_class at finalisation. Two faces of one cause: (a) an approved delivery whose verdict already promoted (M6-07 -- the verdict IS the ladder's input) has a second promote queued on its ship decision; (b) an AGT-609 re-grade, whose verdict says in writing 'the ladder not asked' and carries ladder_applied_at NULL, spawns a ship decision carrying bug_fix anyway -- so a 'verdict already stamped' test alone would NOT suppress it. Rung 3 / streak 5 on bug_fix was bought partly by this. / Have record_ship_decision() ask the verdict it already loaded: pass ladder_work_class NULL when the verdict's ladder_applied_at is set (the ladder has had this delivery) OR when the verdict declines the ladder (auto_done_eligible false / the AGT-609 re-grade reason -- better, an explicit p_ladder flag regrade-current.js sets), and keep the demote-on-reverse path for the one decision that does carry a class. Guard both directions: a plain approved ship still promotes exactly once, a re-grade promotes nothing. Do NOT rewind the 54 deliveries already counted twice: trust counters run forward only and history is not retroactively rewound (pattern:160). Land this BEFORE the sweep repair, or the 78 queued promotes release together. (architect, 2026-11-09)

## b790bb6e0608cf79 · other · high · ticketed

**Fact:** A promotion bar exists so a finding reaches a human or a ruling capability once it is real, not once per cycle; an ask already ruled is answered, and re-asking it spends a judgment-lane call to re-derive a stored answer.

**Locations:**
- `scripts/staff-watch.js:65` — "asksToFile() (AGT-172) counts only an OPEN runner_card_asks row as standing, so an ask already answered `no` is not seen as standing and is filed again on the next --promote --apply"
- `runner_card_asks` — "the same 15 fingerprints have been ruled 410 times since 2026-09-29, every one of them most recently on 2026-11-08, and this cycle's (7g) ruled the same 15 again -- all 15 `no`, several of them for the 43rd time"
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md (7d)/(7g)` — "the tail runs --promote --apply and then design-ruling every cycle, so the loop costs one judgment-lane sub-agent run per cycle for an answer the ledger already holds"

**Proposed resolution:** Make asksToFile() treat a RULED ask as standing for its fingerprint, not only an open one -- so a `no` suppresses re-filing until the evidence changes (a new cycle count crossing the bar, or a different detail), the same way record_skip() bumps a count instead of adding a row. Found by this cycle's own (7g) Designer ruling, which reported the 410 and correctly filed nothing itself because only the Governance Architect files.

**Ruling:** scripts/staff-watch.js builds its standing set from one read -- `runner_card_asks?target_kind=eq.skill-edit&answer=is.null` -- and asksToFile() then marks a promotion `standing` only if its fingerprint is in that set. AGT-172 chose that deliberately and says so in the file: 'ONLY AN UNANSWERED ASK SUPPRESSES ... which is the difference between a dedupe and a mute.' That reasoning holds while John is the answerer, and it has stopped holding: all 425 answered rows were written by a cycle (44 distinct answered_cycle values) and none by hand, so an automated ruling lane is re-deriving a stored answer rather than a human seeing a recurrence. Live count: 422 answered asks since 2026-09-29 over exactly 15 fingerprints, 407 of them answered 'no', the top three at 44 asks each, and all 15 asked again on 2026-11-08 -- one full re-ask of the whole set, which the tail then rules in (7g) at one judgment-lane call per cycle. The promotion bar exists so a finding reaches a ruler once it is real, not once per cycle. / Key the standing read on the fingerprint's RULING, not on the open row: a ruled ask suppresses re-filing for its fingerprint until the evidence changes -- a new distinct-cycle count crossing the bar, or a different detail -- and the recurrence bumps a count on the standing row the way record_skip() already bumps a skip instead of adding a row. Keep AGT-172's mute/dedupe distinction by making the trigger the EVIDENCE rather than the answer: a fingerprint whose cycle count has moved since its last ruling is genuinely new and still files. Assert both directions, which costs no build to check (below): the 15 ruled fingerprints file nothing, and a fingerprint with no prior ask still files. Leave the uniq_card_ask constraint where it is -- it is the in-run backstop, not the guard. (architect, 2026-11-09)

**Fact:** Whether one approved delivery feeds the ladder once (its verdict) or again when its ship decision finalises: AGT-521's verdict promoted bug_fix 4->5 / rung 2->3, and ship decision 12b6915e holds a second unstamped promote for 7b; live, 49 deliveries were counted twice and 51 more are queued.

**Locations:**
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:3054-3058` — "THE VERDICT IS THE LADDER'S INPUT (`M6-07`, `SES-122` (a), `v7.0.397`) — run this the moment the verifier prints `recorded as runner_verdicts <id>`:** an `approve` promotes the ticket's work class (streak +1, and a rung on every fifth) [...] and the call is idempotent per verdict, so a re-run counts nothing twice."
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:4290-4291` — "It finalises every `open` decision past its `expires_at` and promotes the work class each one named (`SES-107`'s streak rule; a class is promoted once, ever — `ladder_applied_at` is the stamp that enforces it)."
- `public.sweep_decision_windows(uuid,text)` — "if r.ladder_work_class is not null and r.ladder_applied_at is null then -- M6-07: an unreversed decision past its window IS the promote signal. [...] from public.ladder_apply_signal(r.ladder_work_class, 'promote', p_actor_cycle, p_actor_session);"
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:970-972` — "counting the tap as well as the verdict counts one delivery twice, and a double count does not merely look wrong — it manufactures a rung, which buys real extra files, real extra tasks and the auto-done bar."
- `runner_verdicts:5a759cfc-c7fc-4d8c-b749-205511eca37f` — "backlog_id AGT-521, verdict approve, ladder_applied_at 2026-11-09T10:28:44.557042+00:00"
- `runner_ladder:bug_fix` — "work_class bug_fix, rung 3, streak 5, updated_at 2026-11-09T10:28:44.557042+00:00"
- `runner_decisions:12b6915e-edae-4831-ae6a-0d6c71979012` — "kind ship, backlog_id AGT-521, ladder_work_class bug_fix, ladder_applied_at null, status open, expires_at 2026-11-12T10:29:38.680629+00:00"
- `runner_cycles:828a6ded-40ef-4a1a-8b2f-c8ff726d7c96` — "verdict_ladder_signal promote: bug_fix streak 4->5, rung 2->3"

**Proposed resolution:** SES-122a / SES-315(b) should win (the verdict is the ladder's input; one delivery, one count): sweep_decision_windows() skips the promote for a ship decision whose verdict row is already stamped, or record_ship_decision() passes NULL ladder_work_class when the verdict is stamped, keeping the demote on reverse. Land it before the filed sweep repair, or 51 manufactured promotions release at once.

**Ruling:** public.record_ship_decision() reads the ticket's priority_class off the board and sets v_wc := ladder_work_class(v_class) UNCONDITIONALLY -- its source never reads the verdict's ladder_applied_at or auto_done_eligible, although it already holds the whole verdict row. sweep_decision_windows() then promotes any unstamped ladder_work_class at finalisation. Two faces of one cause: (a) an approved delivery whose verdict already promoted (M6-07 -- the verdict IS the ladder's input) has a second promote queued on its ship decision; (b) an AGT-609 re-grade, whose verdict says in writing 'the ladder not asked' and carries ladder_applied_at NULL, spawns a ship decision carrying bug_fix anyway -- so a 'verdict already stamped' test alone would NOT suppress it. Rung 3 / streak 5 on bug_fix was bought partly by this. / Have record_ship_decision() ask the verdict it already loaded: pass ladder_work_class NULL when the verdict's ladder_applied_at is set (the ladder has had this delivery) OR when the verdict declines the ladder (auto_done_eligible false / the AGT-609 re-grade reason -- better, an explicit p_ladder flag regrade-current.js sets), and keep the demote-on-reverse path for the one decision that does carry a class. Guard both directions: a plain approved ship still promotes exactly once, a re-grade promotes nothing. Do NOT rewind the 54 deliveries already counted twice: trust counters run forward only and history is not retroactively rewound (pattern:160). Land this BEFORE the sweep repair, or the 78 queued promotes release together. (architect, 2026-11-09)

## 0312da6c0e3ef18b · other · medium · ticketed

**Fact:** A ticket whose build adds a regression test can never satisfy AGT-457's baseline/graded-set equality on its first verifier run: pre-build-baseline.js measures the related set of the kickoff's declared files BEFORE the new test file exists, so the baseline is one name narrower than the graded set and verifier.js exits 2 recording nothing. The only way through is re-measuring the baseline post-build, which is no longer a pre-build measurement for the new file.

**Locations:**
- `/home/user/deepbench-frontend/scripts/verifier.js` — "verifier: baseline NARROWER than the set being graded: 1 of the 13 graded tests is absent from the 12 tests the baseline measured (AGT-457)."
- `/home/user/deepbench-frontend/docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:2918` — "node scripts/pre-build-baseline.js --kickoff=<the kickoff_path> --out=$S/pre-build-baseline-<your cycle id>.txt"

**Proposed resolution:** Let pre-build-baseline.js accept the kickoff's declared NEW test files as baseline entries with an explicit `absent pre-build` marker, or have verifier.js treat a graded test that the kickoff declares as new -- and that reads green -- as covered rather than unmeasured, so AGT-457 still fires on a genuinely unmeasured red.

**Ruling:** scripts/pre-build-baseline.js measures the related set of the kickoff's declared files against the PRE-build tree, so a test file the build is about to create cannot be in it. verifier.js's baselineCoverageFinding() (AGT-457) then refuses any baseline narrower than the set being graded -- exit 2, baseline-narrower-than-graded-set, nothing recorded -- although the missing name is a brand-new test that reads green. The only way through is re-measuring the baseline after the build, which is no longer a pre-build measurement, so the rule as shipped is unsatisfiable for every test-adding ticket. / Let the instrument say what it could not have measured. pre-build-baseline.js already has the name: emit each kickoff-declared test file absent from the pre-build tree as a baseline entry marked 'absent pre-build', and have verifier.js treat a graded test that the kickoff declared NEW and that reads green as COVERED (it already has the neverMeasured bucket) rather than as a narrower baseline. AGT-457's refusal must still fire on a genuinely unmeasured RED, which is the case to keep in the test. (architect, 2026-11-09)

## dda704e6aafa2710 · other · medium · ticketed

**Fact:** Step 5 statement (1) tells every cycle to class the queue top through capability classify-ticket when supports_class IS NULL, but no per-cycle driver exists for it: agent-prompt.js only assembles the prompt, and api/_lib/handlers/prioritizer-write.js (the only sanctioned writer) is reachable in-process from scripts/rank-backlog.js, which refuses once a day has had its re-rank, and from the one-off scripts/prioritizer-first-run.mjs. AGT-521 was picked and built with supports_class NULL and no classify pass was possible.

**Locations:**
- `/home/user/deepbench-frontend/docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md:2045` — "--     Run it through the executor, capability `classify-ticket`, agent `prioritizer` -- never by hand"
- `/home/user/deepbench-frontend/scripts/rank-backlog.js:112` — "import { handle as prioritizerWrite } from %27../api/_lib/handlers/prioritizer-write.js%27;"

**Proposed resolution:** Either give classify-ticket its own per-cycle driver (the rank-backlog two-pass shape, scoped to one ticket) or let rank-backlog.js run its classify half when the day's re-rank has already happened, so the queue top can be served-classed on the cycle that picks it.

**Ruling:** The runbook's step 5 statement (1) tells every cycle to class the queue top through capability classify-ticket when supports_class IS NULL, but nothing in the repo can drive it. scripts/agent-prompt.js only assembles the prompt; the one sanctioned writer, api/_lib/handlers/prioritizer-write.js, is reachable in-process from scripts/rank-backlog.js -- which refuses once that America/Chicago day has had its re-rank -- and from the one-off scripts/prioritizer-first-run.mjs. So the instruction is unperformable on any cycle that picks after the daily re-rank, and the gap is silent: the ticket is built unclassed. / Give the capability a per-cycle driver in the rank-backlog two-pass shape, scoped to ONE ticket: read the queue top, assemble the classify prompt through the executor, and hand the answer to prioritizer-write in-process -- separate from the once-a-day re-rank gate, which exists to stop a whole-board re-rank, not a single ticket's class. Alternatively let rank-backlog.js run its classify half after the day's re-rank has happened. Either way the cycle that picks a ticket can class it before building it. (architect, 2026-11-09)
